task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:

turns.thought:
I've found your account and identified the line that's having trouble. Here's what I'm seeing:

**Line 555-123-2002 (your line):**
- Status: Active
- Plan: Premium Plan — 15.0 GB data limit
- Data used this cycle: **15.1 GB** (your cycle ends 2025-02-28)
- International roaming: **already enabled** (good, since you're in France)

So there are two pieces of good news: your line is active and not suspended, and roaming is already switched on so that part is all set.

The problem is that **you've used 15.1 GB of your 15.0 GB monthly allowance** — you're right at/over your data limit. That's why your mobile data either cuts out completely or crawls along.

To get your data working again for the rest of this cycle, I can "refuel" (add) extra data to your line. On the Premium Plan, refueling costs **$2.00 per GB**, and the maximum I can add is 2 GB.

Before I apply anything, **how much data would you like me to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?**

One note: this charge will be added to your upcoming bill, and it only covers you through the end of this billing cycle (2025-02-28), when your allowance resets.
turns.execution_output:
User: Two gigabytes, please — the 2 GB for $4.00. I want to make sure I have enough to actually use my phone while I'm here.

That will go on my next bill, you said? That's fine. But... will that definitely make my internet fast again? I really need it to work properly — not just a little bit better, but properly fast. I take a lot of photos of my grandchildren and I like to send them on.

turns.thought:
Good news — that's done. I've added **2 GB of data to your line 555-123-2002 for $4.00**, and that charge will appear on your next bill. Your line now has 2 GB of refueled data available on top of your allowance, so the cut-off caused by going over your 15 GB limit is fixed.

To be straight with you though: **I can't promise "fast" — I can promise "working."** Refueling restores your data connection, which was being shut off or throttled because you'd hit your limit. But actual speed also depends on things I can't see from your account:

- The strength and type of the roaming network you're connected to in France
- A few settings on the phone itself

Since you're abroad, the most likely culprit beyond the data limit is that **data roaming may be switched off on the phone handset itself**. I've confirmed roaming is enabled on your *line* (that's the account side, and it was already on), but the phone has its own separate roaming switch, and both need to be on for data to work outside your home network.

Could you check a few things on your phone and let me know what you see? We'll go one step at a time:

1. **Status bar** (the very top of your screen): what icons do you see? In particular — is there a signal strength symbol, and does it say something like 5G, LTE, or 4G? Also, do you see an aeroplane symbol (Airplane Mode) or a "🔽"-style Data Saver icon?
2. **Settings → Mobile/Cellular Data**: is mobile data turned **on**?
3. **Settings → Mobile/Cellular Data → Data Roaming**: is data roaming turned **on**?

Once you tell me what you find, I'll guide you through the next step — and I'll also help you get picture messaging working, since I know sending those photos of your grandchildren matters to you.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me look at my phone... I'll check those things for you.

turns.thought:
Yes — that aeroplane symbol is almost certainly the whole problem. Airplane Mode switches off *all* the phone's wireless radios at once: cellular, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. That perfectly explains why you have no signal bars, no 4G/5G, no data, and no network type at all. It's very easy to switch on by accident, so please don't worry.

And I completely understand being cautious. Let me reassure you on two points:

- **Turning it off is completely safe.** It just switches those radios back on. It won't erase anything, cost you anything, or change any of your settings or photos. It's fully reversible — you can turn it straight back on if you ever want to.
- **The 2 GB I added is still there waiting for you.** It hasn't gone anywhere; your phone just couldn't reach the network to use it.

Please do this:

1. Go back to that same **"Airplane Mode"** screen you found.
2. Tap the switch so that Airplane Mode turns **OFF** (the aeroplane symbol at the top of the screen should disappear).
3. Wait about 30 seconds. Phones need a moment to go searching for a network again, and since you're in France it will be connecting to a roaming partner network, which can take a little longer than at home.
4. Check the top of your screen again.

**Then tell me what you see at the top of your screen.** I'm looking for:

- Signal bars — any at all?
- A network type, like 5G, LTE, or 4G?
- Whether a data symbol has appeared

Don't change anything else yet — not the mobile data switch and not the data roaming switch. I'd like to see what the phone does after just this one change, because it's possible the other two were showing "No" simply *because* Airplane Mode was overriding everything, and they may well come back on by themselves.

Once you tell me what the status bar looks like, I'll walk you through the next single step — and we'll get those photos of your grandchildren sending again.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try that. Turning the aeroplane thing off now...

turns.thought:
That's excellent progress — really good news. Airplane Mode was indeed the main culprit, and your phone is now connected to a **5G network with excellent signal**. That means your SIM is working and you have a strong connection to a roaming partner in France.

You're right that the other two didn't come back on by themselves — some phones keep those switches exactly as you left them. So we'll turn them on manually, one at a time.

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data ON**

1. Go to **Settings**
2. Tap **Mobile Data** (on some phones it's called **Cellular** or **Mobile Network**)
3. Tap the switch so **Mobile Data** turns **ON**

Give it about 30 seconds, then check the top of your screen — that little "data disabled" symbol should disappear.

Please tell me what you see after that, and we'll do the roaming switch as step 2.

**A couple of reassurances before you continue:**

- **This won't cost you anything.** The 2 GB of data I added ($4.00 on your next bill) is what you'll be using — there's no separate charge for switching these on.
- **Mobile data is separate from your mobile plan's calls and texts.** Turning it on just lets your phone use the network for internet — it doesn't change your plan or your number.
- **You're safe to use data in France.** I've confirmed roaming is already enabled on your line on the account side, so the network will accept you there.

One more thing I want to flag, since it came up: your **battery is at 80%**, which is fine for now, but mobile data — especially on 5G while roaming — does use noticeably more battery than normal. If you're out all day taking photos, you might want to keep an eye on it.

Take your time with step 1, and let me know how you get on.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll turn the mobile data on now.

turns.thought:
Great — mobile data is on and your phone is connected to 5G with excellent signal. And to answer your question directly:

**Yes, turn data roaming on next — you'll need it.** Since you're in France, your phone is using a partner network rather than our own. Even with roaming enabled on your line (which I've confirmed is already switched on at the account level), the phone's own roaming switch also has to be on. Both are required, and right now the phone's is off — so that's very likely the last thing standing between you and working internet.

**Please do this:**

1. Go to **Settings → Mobile Data** (or **Cellular / Mobile Network**) — the same screen you were just on
2. Find **Data Roaming**
3. Tap the switch so it turns **ON**
4. You may get a warning message about roaming charges — that's a standard message, and it's fine to accept. There's no extra charge for switching it on; you'll simply be using the 2 GB I added ($4.00 on your next bill)
5. Wait about 30 seconds, then check the top of your screen

**Now, about that downward arrow — yes, that's Data Saver.** It isn't harmful or dangerous, but I do recommend turning it off, and here's why:

Data Saver restricts apps from using data in the background and can slow things down. More importantly for you, it can **stop your photos from sending properly** in the background — which is exactly what you want to be doing with pictures of your grandchildren. Since you specifically want things to work *properly fast*, it's worth switching off.

**So let's do them in this order — roaming first (more urgent), then Data Saver:**

Once you've turned roaming on, go back to **Settings → Mobile Data → Data Saver** (it might be under a "Data Usage" section) and switch it **OFF**.

Then test things out:

- Open a web browser and load a page
- Try sending one photo to see whether it goes through

**Please tell me:**

1. Whether roaming switched on without trouble, and what's at the top of your screen now
2. Whether Data Saver is off
3. Whether a web page loads, and whether your photo sends

If a page loads and the photo goes, we're done. If either doesn't work, tell me exactly what happens — whether it fails instantly, hangs, or gives an error — and I'll take it from there. And if your picture messages still won't send even once data is working, I can walk you through the picture-messaging settings specifically.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll do the roaming one first — I can only manage one thing at a time, I'm afraid. Turning data roaming on now...

turns.thought:
Yes — let's turn Data Saver off now. Everything else is exactly as it should be: Airplane Mode off, SIM active, excellent 5G signal, mobile data on, and data roaming on. Data Saver is the last thing switched on that could be holding you back.

**Please do this:**

1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Mobile Data** (or **Cellular / Mobile Network**) — the same area you've been in
3. Look for **Data Saver** — it may instead be inside a section called **Data Usage** or **Data Saving**
4. Tap the switch so Data Saver turns **OFF**

The downward arrow at the top of your screen should disappear.

**Then let's actually test it**, because that's the real proof:

1. Open your web browser and load any page — does it come up, and does it feel quick?
2. Try sending one of the photos of your grandchildren — does it send?

**Please tell me:**

- Whether the downward arrow is gone
- Whether a web page loads, and how fast it feels (quick, or still sluggish?)
- Whether your photo sends — and if not, what exactly happens (does it fail immediately, spin forever, or show an error?)

A quick note on why this matters for your photos specifically: Data Saver limits background data use, and picture messages often rely on that. So switching it off may make the difference between a photo that appears to send but never quite goes through, and one that sends properly.

If the photos still don't send once everything else is working, don't worry — there are a couple of picture-messaging-specific settings I can walk you through, including checking your messaging app has the right permissions and what's called your MMSC (picture messaging) settings. We'll take that step by step if we need it.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, turning Data Saver off now.

turns.thought:
Yes, go ahead and try loading a webpage now — everything on the settings side is exactly where it should be, so this is the real test.

There's nothing else I need checked first. Please try **both** of these:

1. **Open your browser** and load any page — does it come up, and does it feel quick or still sluggish?
2. **Try sending one photo** of your grandchildren — this is the one that matters most to you

turns.thought:
I'm so glad it's all working — and the photo sending is the best possible confirmation. You did brilliantly working through those settings; that's genuinely fiddly stuff, and you followed it step by step without any trouble at all.

**To answer your questions directly:**

**No, you don't need to change anything else.** Your phone is in exactly the right state now:

- Airplane Mode: off
- SIM: active
- Signal: excellent, on 5G
- Mobile data: on
- Data roaming: on
- Data Saver: off

**And yes, that's correct about the $4.00.** I've just checked your account to be certain, and I can see it sitting on your **next bill (B1003)** — listed as *"Data refueling: 2 GB at $2.0/GB — $4.00,"* dated today. That bill is still in draft; it's issued on 1 March and due on 15 March 2025. So nothing to pay today.

**A couple of things worth knowing before you carry on:**

- **Your 2 GB covers you until 28 February**, which is when your monthly allowance resets and your 15 GB starts fresh. If you get close to using it up while you're still in France, just let me know and I can add more — the maximum per top-up is 2 GB, still $2.00 per GB.
- **Nothing changed on your plan** — this was a one-off data top-up, not a plan change. Your Premium Plan is untouched, and switching data roaming on in your phone settings carries no charge of its own.
- **Do keep an eye on your battery.** You've been at 80%, and 5G data while roaming drains a phone faster than usual — worth having a charger with you on long days out.

Enjoy the rest of your trip, and enjoy showing off those photos of your grandchildren. If your data slows down again or anything else comes up while you're away, just get in touch and I'll help you straight away.
